title: Dominic and the Orbit
premise: Vesper Villalobos, a clone carrying her predecessor's memories and her unsolved murder case, pilots the last courier run between two colony worlds that cut contact after a fleet coup. When children on both worlds begin dreaming the same dream — a relay station at the edge of dead space broadcasting a signal that shouldn't exist — Vesper realizes the dream is a message from someone hiding at the relay, possibly the original Vesper's killer, possibly her original herself. Racing the fleet's expiring truce, she must reach the relay before it goes dark forever, choosing between the duty that defines her and the truth that could reignite war. She reaches the relay, exposes the fleet's manufactured murder, and reopens the channel between worlds — at the cost of the man who loved her original and came to love her.
about_author: Elodie Thackeray is a former radio astronomer who left research to write fiction about the silences between signals. She writes from a decommissioned listening post on the Atlantic coast, where she claims the static helps her plot.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She flies the courier run between worlds Meridian and Halcyon, cataloguing the routines she inherited from her original — including the unsolved murder file she's forbidden to close. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the ache of living someone else's life.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A customs audit forces her to open the murder file in transit; she discovers the victim was the fleet officer who ordered the worlds' communications severed. Beat: first crack in her obedience — the case doesn't add up.

chapters.title: Children of Two Skies
chapters.summary: Dual POV, a Meridian schoolteacher and a Halcyon dock worker. Children on both worlds wake describing the same dream: a spinning relay, a woman's voice counting down. Beat: wonder curdling into institutional fear as officials confiscate the children's drawings.

chapters.title: The Truce Ledger
chapters.summary: Fleet Commander Ashgrave's POV. He reviews the truce countdown and the sealed orders regarding the relay; a subordinate asks why a dead station needs guarding. Beat: cold menace, the machinery of power hiding its purpose.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A stowaway — a Halcyon child who dreamed the dream — is found aboard her ship. The child hums a sequence Vesper recognizes from the murder file's evidence logs. Beat: dread and tenderness intertwined.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, memory sequences. She interrogates her inherited memories and finds gaps — someone edited her clone-line's recollection. Beat: betrayal by her own makers; loyalty to her original begins to curdle into suspicion.

chapters.title: Signal in Dead Space
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She diverts toward the relay against protocol, and the ship's ancient receiver catches a fragment: her original's voice, alive, counting. Beat: vertigo of hope — the dead may not be dead.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV. He offers Vesper a pardon and a new identity if she turns back and reports the child stowaway. Beat: temptation framed as mercy; she sees the leash inside the gift.

chapters.title: The Child's Map
chapters.summary: Vesper and the stowaway, Ilo, share POV. Ilo draws the relay's interior from the dream — including a room that appears in no schematic but exists in the murder file's crime scene photos. Beat: the dream is memory, transmitted.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A fleet picket forces her down on a derelict mining platform; she escapes by scuttling her cargo and burning her own flight record. Beat: the point of no return — she becomes a fugitive in truth.

chapters.title: The Man Who Waited
chapters.summary: New POV: Dorian Reyes, the original Vesper's partner, now a disgraced investigator living on Meridian. He receives her smuggled message and chooses to believe the clone over the fleet. Beat: grief rekindled into purpose; love finding its second shape.

chapters.title: Two Couriers
chapters.summary: Alternating Vesper and Dorian POV as he charters a rusted freighter to intercept her. Their first transmission is stilted, painful — he keeps reaching for the woman she isn't. Beat: the theme made flesh: loyalty to a ghost vs. truth of the person present.

chapters.title: The Dream Deepens
chapters.summary: Ilo's POV. The children's shared dream now includes the countdown's final numbers and a face: Ashgrave's, younger, standing over the murder victim. Beat: horror — the dream is testimony.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's Confession, Unspoken
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn he killed the officer not for power but to bury evidence that the fleet manufactured the war that justified the truce. Beat: corruption revealed as cowardice; he orders the relay destroyed.

chapters.title: Dead Space Crossing
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The final approach: no beacons, no rescue, Ilo navigating by the dream. Dorian's freighter rendezvouses mid-void, and the three run dark together. Beat: fragile found-family forged in silence.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. They board the relay and find her original — alive, half-mad, transmitting the dream for years to anyone who might listen. Beat: devastating reunion; the original is dying and asks the clone to finish her case.

chapters.title: Testimony of the Dying
chapters.summary: Original Vesper's POV. Her full account: the murder, the edited memories, the evidence cached in the relay's core. She asks the clone to broadcast it, knowing it may restart the war to end the lie. Beat: love against duty, inverted — the duty is the lie.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ashgrave's strike force arrives as the truce expires; the relay's shields fail. Dorian holds the transmitter room while Vesper uploads the evidence; Ilo's dream-guidance reroutes the broadcast through the children's network on both worlds. Beat: climax — sacrifice, chaos, the signal going out.

chapters.title: What the Children Heard
chapters.summary: Multi-POV: the schoolteacher, the dock worker, Ashgrave's own daughter. On two worlds, children recite the broadcast in unison; fleets stand down as the lie becomes public. Beat: catharsis through innocence; power collapsing under truth.

chapters.title: The Cost of the Signal
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Dorian is mortally wounded holding the transmitter; he dies believing her, not her original — and tells her so. Beat: grief and grace; love that chose the living woman.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's End
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV. Stripped of command by his own officers, he chooses to surrender the fleet rather than be executed by it — a final act of the cowardice that made him. Beat: power's corruption completing its arc.

chapters.title: The Orbit
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue. She closes the murder file, buries her original beside the relay, and takes the courier route again — now between two worlds that speak. Ilo rides shotgun; the children still dream, but only of stars. Beat: quiet resolution — duty remade as choice, love remade as route.
